rounds.text: Connplex Cinemas Ltd trades at an attractive P/E multiple of 14.9x [E1], while delivering stellar multi-year fundamentals highlighted by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 80% [E8] and profit growth of 151% [E10]. The company's exceptional capital efficiency is underscored by an ROCE of 43.6% [E6] and an ROE of 32.8% [E7], backed by a robust balance sheet featuring a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x [E21] and a comfortable net cash position of INR 7,615 lakhs [E65]. Operational momentum is firing on all cylinders, with footfalls surging roughly 63% year-over-year to 27.63 lakh admits [E61], average ticket prices rising to INR 264 [E62], and spend per head improving to INR 95 [E63]. Furthermore, the business is poised for aggressive expansion, boasting a visible pipeline of over 230 upcoming screens planned across FY27 and FY28 [E57] to scale its footprint beyond the current 113 screens [E55]. Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -60 Cr in Mar 2026 due to upfront expansion costs [E18], institutional money flow reads negative [E27], and the dividend yield sits at 0.00% [E4].

Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E7]. Despite high historical returns on capital, Connplex Cinemas Ltd suffers from a severe disconnect between reported accounting profits and actual cash generation, reporting negative operating cash flow of Rs -60 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -72 Cr in Mar 2026 [E17, E18, E19]. This cash conversion breakdown is reflected in a dismal -2.31x ratio of operating cash flow to reported profit [E17]. Furthermore, working capital requirements have bloated dramatically, with working capital days surging from 108 days to 255 days alongside a stretch in debtor days from 41.9 to 52.7 days [E36, E37]. Operational headwinds are also evident in the 377 bps contraction of EBITDA margin to 23.68% due to higher expansion and operational costs, while employee costs nearly doubled from INR 5.24 crore to INR 9.95 crore [E58, E60]. Compounding these fundamental strains, institutional investors are actively fleeing the stock, with foreign institutional holdings dropping by 1.75 percentage points and domestic institutional holdings falling by 1.12 percentage points, generating a negative institutional money flow signal [E25, E26, E27]. Finally, despite reporting repeated profits, the company pays a 0.00% dividend, leaving shareholders entirely unrewarded while cash is burned on aggressive expansion [E4, E35].

Conceded: [E17], [E18], [E19], [E36], [E37], [E58], [E60]. While cash flow and working capital metrics faced pressure during the aggressive expansion phase, the company maintains a robust net cash position of INR 7,615 lakhs and an almost negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x [E21, E64, E65]. The margin contraction and rising employee costs are a direct and necessary byproduct of scaling the operational footprint to 41 cinemas and 113 screens across 9 states, alongside an accelerated addition of 30 screens in H2FY26 alone [E55, E56, E58, E60]. Far from being unrewarded, shareholders are positioned to benefit from explosive top-line and bottom-line expansion, including a 3-year compounded sales growth of 80% and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 151% [E8, E10]. Institutional outflows [E25, E26, E27] overlook the remarkable fundamental performance driving a 63% YoY increase in total footfalls to 27.63 lakh admits [E61]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF demonstrates that today’s market price of Rs 204 already implies a modest 4.2% earnings growth, offering a massive margin of safety compared to the intrinsic value and the company's strong projected trajectory [E2, E28, E30].

Conceded: [E21, E64, E65] regarding the clean balance sheet and net cash position. However, the bull's attempt to brush off negative cash flows as a mere byproduct of expansion ignores the severity of an operating cash flow burn of Rs -60 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -72 Cr in Mar 2026, translating to a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -2.31x [E17, E18, E19, E20]. While the bull highlights historic 3-year growth metrics [E8, E10], it completely dismisses the immediate reality of margin erosion, such as the 377 bps drop in EBITDA margin and employee costs nearly doubling from INR 5.24 crore to INR 9.95 crore due to scaling [E58, E60]. The bull’s dismissal of institutional outflows [E25, E26, E27] as short-sighted overlooks a massive 2.87 percentage point reduction in institutional holdings, pointing to smart money fleeing the mounting working capital strain where debtor days worsened to 52.7 days and working capital days blew out from 108 to 255 days [E36, E37]. Finally, relying on a reverse DCF [E30] provides cold comfort when the stock trades at zero dividend yield [E4] and sits deep in the lower quintile of its 52-week range at just 20% of its high [E5].

Conceded: [E17, E18, E19, E20] regarding the negative operating and free cash flows in March 2026. However, the bear exaggerates the working capital strain by ignoring that the business operates on a pristine balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x and a comfortable net cash position of INR 7,615 lakhs [E21, E65]. The rise in employee costs and scaling expenses is the direct, intentional cost of a massive footprint expansion that added 30 screens in H2FY26 alone to reach 113 screens across 9 states, driving a 63% year-on-year surge in footfalls to 27.63 lakh admits [E55, E56, E61]. This heavy investment underpins a robust 3-year compounded sales growth of 80% and profit growth of 151% [E8, E10], alongside stellar returns on capital including an ROCE of 43.6% and an ROE of 32.8% [E6, E7]. The bear’s focus on institutional exits and a low 52-week position [E5, E25, E26] misses the fundamental undervaluation highlighted by a reverse DCF showing the current price only requires a modest 4.2% earnings growth against an 18.0% base case [E30].

Conceded: [E21, E65] regarding the low debt-to-equity and net cash position. However, pointing to a pristine balance sheet does not erase the stark reality that operating cash flow collapsed to negative ₹60 crore and free cash flow plunged to negative ₹72 crore in March 2026 [E18, E19], representing a severe cash conversion of negative 2.31x [E17]. The bull defends rising employee costs and capital expenditures as the natural price of scaling 30 screens in H2FY26 [E56, E60], yet this aggressive expansion has severely bloated working capital days from 108 to 255 days alongside a jump in debtor days [E36, E37]. While the bull dismisses institutional outflows [E25, E26], smart money is actively fleeing with negative institutional money flow of 2.87 percentage points [E27], running counter to the narrative of fundamental undervaluation. Furthermore, the company’s yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are flagged as inconsistent [E15, E16], and EBITDA margin actually contracted by 377 basis points year-on-year to 23.68% due to these very expansion-related pressures [E58].
